findings.clinical_note: Markedly elevated LDL, major atherogenic risk; initiate or intensify statin therapy.
Elevated triglycerides contributing to atherogenic dyslipidemia.
Impaired fasting glucose/early diabetes; requires lifestyle and possibly pharmacologic intervention.
Elevated creatinine indicating mild renal dysfunction.
Mildly reduced GFR, consistent with early renal impairment.
Low-normal CO2 suggesting possible mild metabolic acidosis; monitor electrolytes and acid-base status.
Low HDL adds to cardiovascular risk; encourage exercise and dietary modification.

panel_patterns.interpretation: Atherogenic dyslipidemia with elevated LDL, total cholesterol, triglycerides and low‑normal HDL, conferring high ASCVD risk.
Impaired fasting glucose with diabetic range A1c, indicating established diabetes mellitus requiring treatment.
Mild renal impairment evidenced by elevated creatinine and reduced eGFR; monitor renal function and avoid nephrotoxins.

overall_assessment: The patient exhibits severe dyslipidemia (high LDL, total cholesterol, triglycerides) and diabetic range hyperglycemia (elevated fasting glucose and A1c), placing them at high cardiovascular risk. Mild renal dysfunction is present (creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, eGFR 86). Low‑normal CO2 may signal a developing metabolic acidosis. Priorities are aggressive lipid lowering (statin therapy), diabetes management, and close monitoring of renal function and acid‑base status. Lifestyle modification and cardiovascular risk reduction are essential.
data_gaps: Liver function tests (ALT, AST, ALP, bilirubin) not available
